concepts.title: Secant and Tangent Definitions
concepts.definition: A straight line in a plane can cross a circle at two points as a secant, touch it at one single point as a tangent, or share no common points.
concepts.key_idea: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point, representing a limiting case of a secant.

solution_steps.action: Count the number of points of intersection between the line and the circle
solution_steps.explain: A non-intersecting line has 0 common points, a tangent has 1 common point, and a secant has 2 common points.

solution_steps.action: Classify the line based on point count
solution_steps.explain: If the intersection count is exactly 1, the line is a tangent to the circle.

solution_steps.explain: Conclude whether the line is a secant (2 points), tangent (1 point), or non-intersecting (0 points) based on the classification.

concepts.title: Perpendicularity of Radius and Tangent
concepts.definition: The radius drawn to the point of contact of a tangent line is perpendicular to that tangent line.
concepts.key_idea: The point of contact is the closest point on the tangent line to the circle center.

solution_steps.action: Select an arbitrary point Q on the tangent line XY other than the point of contact P
solution_steps.explain: Point Q must lie outside the circle because XY touches the circle only at P.

solution_steps.action: Compare distance OQ with radius OP
solution_steps.explain: Since Q is outside the circle, OQ is greater than the radius OP.
OP is the shortest distance from centre O to line XY, so OP is perpendicular to XY.

concepts.title: Calculating Tangent Length from External Point
concepts.definition: The tangent length from an external point to a circle is evaluated using the right triangle formed by radius, distance from centre, and tangent segment.
concepts.key_idea: Pythagoras theorem applies to the right triangle formed by radius, tangent, and centre distance.

concepts.title: Calculating Radius from Tangent Length and Distance
concepts.definition: The radius of a circle is computed by taking the square root of the difference between squared distance from centre and squared tangent length.
concepts.key_idea: Radius is one leg of the right triangle formed with tangent segment and centre distance.

concepts.title: Calculating Distance of External Point from Centre
concepts.definition: The distance from circle centre to an external point is calculated as the hypotenuse of the right triangle formed by radius and tangent length.
concepts.key_idea: Hypotenuse equals square root of sum of squared radius and squared tangent length.

concepts.title: Equality of Tangents from External Point
concepts.definition: The lengths of two tangent segments drawn from a single point outside a circle to the circle are equal.
concepts.key_idea: Tangents drawn from the same external point to a circle are congruent.
question_patterns: prove that lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal

solution_steps.action: Construct right triangles formed by centre, external point, and points of contact
solution_steps.explain: Join centre O to external point P, and radii OQ and OR to contact points.
Triangles OQP and ORP are right-angled, share hypotenuse OP, and have equal radii OQ = OR, so they are congruent by RHS.
By CPCT, tangent lengths PQ and PR are equal.

concepts.title: Chord of Outer Concentric Circle Touching Inner Circle
concepts.definition: A chord of a larger concentric circle that is tangent to a smaller concentric circle is bisected at the point of contact, with length derived from both radii.
concepts.key_idea: The radius of the inner circle is perpendicular to and bisects the chord of the outer circle.

concepts.title: Supplementary Angles Between Tangents and at Centre
concepts.definition: The angle formed by two tangents from an external point and the angle subtended by contact radii at the centre are supplementary.
concepts.key_idea: Angles at centre and between tangents sum to 180 degrees in the quadrilateral formed by tangents and radii.

concepts.title: Angle Bisector Property of Centre Line
concepts.definition: The line segment connecting circle centre to an external point bisects the angle between the two tangents drawn from that point.
concepts.key_idea: The line joining centre and external point bisects the angle between tangents.

concepts.title: Properties of Circumscribing Quadrilaterals
concepts.definition: For a quadrilateral drawn around a circle touching all four sides, the sum of lengths of opposite sides is equal.
concepts.key_idea: Equal tangent segments from each vertex lead to equal sums of opposite sides in a circumscribed quadrilateral.

solution_steps.action: Express each side as sum of two tangent segments
solution_steps.explain: Let contact points on sides AB, BC, CD, DA be P, Q, R, S respectively.

solution_steps.action: Apply tangent equality theorem from each vertex
solution_steps.explain: AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS.
AB + CD = (AP + PB) + (CR + RD) = (AS + BQ) + (CQ + DS) = (AS + SD) + (BQ + QC) = AD + BC.

questions: How many tangents can a circle have?

Fill in the blanks: (i) A tangent to a circle intersects it in point(s). (ii) A line intersecting a circle in two points is called a secant. (iii) A circle can have at most two parallel tangents. (iv) The common point of a tangent to a circle and the circle is called point of contact.
A tangent PQ at a point P of a circle of radius 5 cm meets a line through the centre O at a point Q so that OQ = 12 cm. Length PQ is: (A) 12 cm (B) 13 cm (C) 8.5 cm (D) sqrt(119) cm.
Draw a circle and two lines parallel to a given line such that one is a tangent and the other, a secant to the circle.
From a point Q, the length of the tangent to a circle is 24 cm and the distance of Q from the centre is 25 cm. The radius of the circle is (A) 7 cm (B) 12 cm (C) 15 cm (D) 24.5 cm.

If tangents PA and PB from a point P to a circle with centre O are inclined to each other at angle of 80 degrees, then angle POA is equal to (A) 50 degrees (B) 60 degrees (C) 70 degrees (D) 80 degrees.
Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
Prove that the perpendicular at the point of contact to the tangent to a circle passes through the centre.

A quadrilateral ABCD is drawn to circumscribe a circle. Prove that AB + CD = AD + BC.

Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
